seoDescription: Learn how to build a client-side authentication system in your Next.js application using a Strapi backend. This tutorial walks through modifying a navigation component to display a dynamic login form. You'll see how to manage form state with React's `useState` hook, handle user input, and submit credentials to a Strapi API endpoint. Discover how to process the JSON Web Token (JWT) returned from Strapi, store it securely in browser cookies using the `js-cookie` library, and create helper functions to manage the auth state.

chapters.title: Adding Conditional UI for Authentication
chapters.description: This chapter covers adding the JSX to nav.js for conditionally rendering a login form or user-specific links based on a user object.

chapters.title: Handling Form State and User Input
chapters.description: This section explains how to implement the `handleChange` function with dynamic ES6 properties and initialize form state using the `useState` hook.

chapters.title: Submitting Login Data to Strapi
chapters.description: This chapter details how to create an asynchronous `handleSubmit` function to send login credentials to the Strapi `/api/auth/local` endpoint via a POST request.

chapters.title: Managing JWT with an `auth.js` Helper
chapters.description: This chapter introduces a dedicated `lib/auth.js` file for handling JSON Web Tokens, using the `js-cookie` library to set and unset auth cookies.

chapters.title: Finalizing the Login/Logout Flow
chapters.description: This chapter connects the `auth.js` helpers to the navigation component, implements the logout function, and identifies the remaining state variables needed.

summary:
## Dynamic Navigation UI

The navigation component (`nav.js`) is modified to conditionally render different UI elements based on the user's authentication status. 
- If a `user` object exists, it displays **Profile** and **Logout** links.
- If there is no `user`, it displays a **Login form** and a link to **Register**.

## Client-Side Form Handling

Standard React patterns are used to manage the login form.

- **State Management**: The `useState` hook initializes and stores the form data.
  ```javascript
  const [data, setData] = useState({ 
    identifier: '', 
    password: '' 
  });
  ```

- **Input Handling**: A single, clever `handleChange` function updates the state for multiple inputs by using ES6 dynamic property names.
  > [!TIP]
  > Using `[e.target.name]: e.target.value` allows one event handler to manage state for an entire form, reducing boilerplate code.

## Authenticating with Strapi

The `handleSubmit` function orchestrates the login request to the Strapi backend.

- **API Endpoint**: It makes an asynchronous `POST` request to the `/api/auth/local` endpoint provided by Strapi's Users & Permissions plugin.
- **Request Payload**: The function sends a JSON object containing the user's `identifier` (email or username) and `password`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The Strapi API URL should be stored in an environment variable (e.g., `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_STRAPI_URL`) rather than being hardcoded in the component.

## JWT and Cookie Management

A dedicated helper file, `lib/auth.js`, is created to centralize authentication logic.

- **`js-cookie` Library**: This lightweight dependency is used to programmatically set and remove browser cookies.
- **`setToken(data)`**: On successful login, this function extracts the `jwt`, `id`, and `username` from the Strapi response and stores them in cookies.
- **`unsetToken()`**: This function removes the `jwt`, `id`, and `username` cookies.

> [!NOTE]
> After both setting and unsetting the token, the page is programmatically reloaded (`Router.reload()`) to ensure the UI updates to reflect the new authentication state.

## Next Steps

The implementation is not yet complete. The conditional rendering logic relies on `user` and `loading` variables, which are currently undefined. The next video will explain how to provide this state to the navigation component.
